_comment: DP review criteria. Section order follows the Government of Alberta 'Build Your AI Data Centre' approvals pathway so the review maps onto the province's own framework. Criteria marked "origin": "precedent" come from the Loudoun County use-specific standards and the JLARC/WRI impact research — they exist because that evidence says those are the points where applications get contested. Edit freely; the tool reads this file at load.
disclaimer: This checklist is a research aid, not a substitute for reading the current bylaw and regulation text. Confirm every requirement against the governing document before making or recommending a decision. Your notes stay in this browser and are never uploaded.

sections.title: Land use & zoning
sections.intro: Establish the application's footing before assessing anything else. In Alberta this now varies materially between municipalities.

criteria.text: Use class confirmed against the current Land Use Bylaw — permitted or discretionary?
criteria.help: This differs by municipality and has changed recently. Rocky View moved Data Centre Campus to discretionary in July 2026; Sturgeon and Parkland treat data processing as permitted. Discretionary status materially widens your grounds for refusal.

criteria.text: Zoning district correct for the proposed use, and the parcel correctly designated
Any additional plan required (Master Site Development Plan, Area Structure Plan conformity) identified and submitted
criteria.help: Parkland County requires an MSDP in addition to the Development Permit for data processing facilities on the amended lands.

criteria.text: Setbacks meet bylaw minimums, including from road allowances and adjacent parcels
Building height, site coverage and massing assessed against district standards
Screening, buffering and landscaping addressed for adjacent residential or agricultural uses
criteria.help: Loudoun County's use-specific standards treat screening of large windowless buildings as a distinct requirement rather than folding it into general landscaping.

criteria.text: Visual impact of building mass, and of any associated substation, assessed from public vantage points
Site access, road network capacity and construction traffic routing addressed

sections.title: Power & grid
sections.intro: The binding physical constraint in Alberta. An application without a credible grid position is not a near-term project regardless of its land use merits.

criteria.text: Proposed electrical load stated in MW, and consistent across all submitted documents
criteria.help: Building area is a poor proxy for load. Rising rack density means a smaller building can carry a larger grid impact.

criteria.text: Facility classified against the 75 MW 'large data centre' threshold in the Data Centre Regulation
AESO connection status evidenced — tethered, bridged, or untethered
criteria.help: Tethered projects receive AESO assessment priority but cannot obtain system access above their associated generation capacity until that generation is in service.

criteria.text: If bridged: the three-year limit and the curtailment obligation understood and reflected in conditions
criteria.help: Bridged access is temporary, capped at three years, and carries an obligation to reduce consumption when the grid needs the room.

criteria.text: If tethered: the associated generation or storage identified, and its AUC approval status confirmed
criteria.help: Tethered generating or storage units require AUC approval under the Hydro and Electric Energy Act. That is a separate application with its own land use, noise and emissions profile.

criteria.text: Whether on-site generation forms part of this application or a separate one is clearly established
Transmission connection, substation siting and any new line requirements addressed as part of the application
Levy tier noted (2% grid-connected / 1% self-generating / 0% off-grid) as an indicator of the power model
criteria.help: Effective 31 December 2026. The tier an applicant expects is a quick read on how they have structured supply.

sections.title: Water
sections.intro: The impact category that most reliably generates public submissions, and the one where applicant figures most need testing.

criteria.text: Cooling topology stated — closed-loop, evaporative, air-cooled, or immersion
criteria.help: This is the single largest determinant of water demand. Do not accept a consumption figure without knowing the topology behind it.

criteria.text: Annual water consumption quantified, with peak-day demand stated separately
Water source identified — municipal supply, licensed surface water, groundwater, or recycled
Water licence or allocation in place, or the pathway to one identified
Municipal system capacity confirmed if the supply is municipal, including effects on other users
Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) or equivalent metric committed to, with a reporting mechanism
Discharge quality, volume and receiving system addressed
Drought and restriction scenarios addressed — what happens to the facility when allocations are curtailed

sections.title: Noise & air
sections.intro: Steady-state operation and periodic generator testing are different problems. Assess both.

criteria.text: Noise Impact Assessment submitted and measured at the property line, not at the equipment
Compliance demonstrated against AUC Rule 012 where applicable, and against municipal noise standards
Low-frequency noise and tonal components specifically addressed, not just overall dBA
criteria.help: Chiller and fan noise carries low-frequency content that an overall dBA figure can understate. This is a recurring source of complaint in mature data centre jurisdictions.

criteria.text: Cumulative noise assessed where other facilities exist or are approved nearby
Backup generation type, capacity and fuel identified
NOx and other air emissions quantified, including during generator testing
Generator testing schedule proposed, and suitable as a condition
Light spillage from the site and any security lighting addressed

sections.title: Servicing & infrastructure cost recovery
sections.intro: Alberta's stated first commitment is that Albertans do not pay. This section is where that is tested on a specific file.

criteria.text: All project-related infrastructure improvements funded by the developer, with no transfer to municipal ratepayers
criteria.help: Sturgeon County states this explicitly. It is the clearest cost-recovery language among the Alberta municipalities reviewed and a useful benchmark.

criteria.text: Development agreement scope identified — roads, water, wastewater, stormwater
Off-site levies calculated and applied
Stormwater management plan submitted and consistent with provincial and municipal guidelines
Fire protection, emergency access and water supply for firefighting confirmed with the fire authority
Assessment and tax revenue implications understood, including any exemptions claimed
criteria.help: JLARC's Virginia review found incentive returns frequently diverged from projections. Worth establishing the assumption early.

criteria.text: Broadband and fibre routing addressed
Environmental site assessment completed to the stage required
Wetlands, riparian areas and watercourses identified, with the Alberta Wetland Policy applied
Agricultural land impact assessed, including loss of productive land and fragmentation
Wildlife and habitat considerations addressed
Historical resources clearance obtained where required
Public lands interface addressed if applicable
Pipeline and utility rights-of-way identified, with setbacks respected
Reclamation and soil handling during construction addressed

sections.title: Community & consultation
sections.intro: Anticipate the submissions rather than receive them. The impact research in the Precedents section is the best guide to what will be raised.

criteria.text: Indigenous consultation undertaken, and the record adequate
criteria.help: Listed in the province's own approvals pathway. Confirm the Crown's consultation obligations have been discharged where they apply.

criteria.text: Public notification completed per statutory requirements
Adjacent landowners identified and notified, including across municipal boundaries where relevant
Applicant-led engagement undertaken, with the record submitted
Submissions received catalogued by theme — water, noise, traffic, property value, land loss
Employment and local economic claims tested rather than accepted as stated
criteria.help: Operating employment at data centres is typically far lower than construction employment. Confirm which figure is being quoted.

criteria.text: Cumulative effects considered where multiple facilities are proposed or approved in the area

sections.title: Decommissioning & end-of-life
sections.intro: Rarely addressed in current Alberta bylaws, and the gap most likely to matter in twenty years.

criteria.text: Expected facility life and technology refresh cycle stated
Decommissioning plan required as a condition, or a reason recorded for not requiring one
Security or bonding for site restoration considered
Adaptive reuse or demolition pathway identified for the building and any substation
Responsibility for the associated generation asset at end-of-life established if the project is tethered
